outcome: The general QUE conjecture of Rudnick and Sarnak — that all high-frequency Laplace eigenfunctions on a compact negatively-curved manifold equidistribute — remains completely open for arbitrary negatively-curved manifolds; only the arithmetic special case (already resolved before the frozen date by Lindenstrauss and Soundararajan) has seen further extension, to products of hyperbolic 2- and 3-spaces, and that extension is itself a variant/special case rather than a case of the general conjecture as stated in the bullet.
summary: The bullet states the general Rudnick–Sarnak QUE conjecture for arbitrary compact negatively-curved manifolds. This remains fully open: the current Wikipedia article on quantum unique ergodicity (checked live for context, not as a research source) discusses only the weaker quantum ergodicity theorem (Shnirelman/Zelditch/Colin de Verdière), which guarantees equidistribution for a density-one subsequence of eigenfunctions, not all of them, and does not report any resolution of the full QUE conjecture. Searches for progress since 26 January 2024 turned up three genuine results, none of which bear on the general conjecture as stated: (1) Shem-Tov and Silberman, 'Arithmetic quantum unique ergodicity for products of hyperbolic 2- and 3-spaces' (arXiv:2206.05955), first posted 2022-06-13, with a revised v2 posted 2025-01-26 and a 2025 journal publication in the Journal d'Analyse Mathématique — this proves AQUE (the arithmetic special case, using Hecke operators) for a specific class of arithmetic locally symmetric spaces; AQUE for the classical case (surfaces) was already settled by Lindenstrauss (2006) and Soundararajan (2010), well before the frozen revision, so even this is an extension of an already-resolved arithmetic sub-problem, not progress on the stated (non-arithmetic, general) conjecture, and per §3.1 counts as a related/variant result rather than a case of this bullet's conjecture; (2) Kim and Miller, 'Semiclassical Measures on Hyperbolic Manifolds' (arXiv:2503.01528, March 2025), which constrains the support of semiclassical measures (showing supports must contain the cosphere bundle of a totally geodesic submanifold) but explicitly does not resolve QUE — it is a related but distinct question about possible limit measures, not a proof or disproof of equidistribution; (3) an arXiv paper on QUE for magnetic Laplacians on the flat torus T^2 (arXiv:2411.18449, November 2024) which is a different operator on a non-negatively-curved space entirely. No AI or machine-learning involvement was found in connection with any of this work; broader searches for AI/ML activity touching QUE returned only unrelated physics applications (quantum-enhanced LLMs, quantum-informed ML for chaotic-system prediction) that use 'quantum' and 'chaos' in an unrelated sense and have nothing to do with the Rudnick–Sarnak conjecture. The record is therefore 'open' with no_change_found true.
competing_reading: One could argue the Shem-Tov–Silberman extension to products of hyperbolic 2- and 3-spaces is a 'case' of the general QUE conjecture (since products of hyperbolic spaces are themselves negatively-curved-in-each-factor locally symmetric spaces) rather than a mere variant, which would make it `partial` progress with `resolution_direction` confirmed. I read it instead as confined to the arithmetic sub-conjecture (it relies essentially on Hecke operators, which have no analogue for a generic negatively-curved manifold), so it does not narrow the general conjecture's territory the way, e.g., resolving QUE for a specific non-arithmetic manifold would.
what_would_settle_it: A result proving or disproving equidistribution of eigenfunctions for a negatively-curved manifold or family of manifolds without reliance on arithmetic/Hecke structure would settle whether this counts as genuine progress on the stated (general) conjecture; absent that, the arithmetic-only results stay out of scope.
